subject: Inference ops options and costing questions

Subject: Inference ops options and costing questions

Hi Sam — great to meet on the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap:
- OptiRail primary use: real-time train diagnostics + automated crew messaging. Tight p95 latency target (~200ms) for alerts; bursts during peak ops (3x baseline for ~30–60m).
- Data sensitivity: operational data, PII in limited fields. Customer needs SOC2 and KMS control; might consider VPC/private deployment if procurement requires.
- Expected volume: rough starting estimate 100M tokens/month (will refine).

Deployment modes we discussed (quick pros/cons):
- Hosted API: fastest to production, per-token pricing, auto-scaling for bursts, no infra ops for you.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools (monthly commit) for predictable latency & throughput—better unit economics if steady high volume.
- Private/VPC or on-prem: for strict network control and KMS/HSM integration; higher setup effort and a different license model.

Open items we need from you to produce a tailored costing sheet: 
1) Clarify 100M tokens: is that steady, or an average with 3x peak bursts?
2) Target p95 and acceptable cold-start latency (for hosted).
3) Any firm procurement/q4 closure dates or constraints.

Next steps I propose: 
- I’ll pull together a short costing sketch (hosted per-token vs. dedicated commit tiers vs private deployment outline) and share an editable sheet. Marcus will include a sample reserved-tier pricing.
- If helpful, schedule a 45-min pricing deep-dive next week to walk numbers and tradeoffs.
- We’ll attach SOC2 snapshot and our hosted vs dedicated one-pager for compliance review.

Attaching: redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-one-pager.pdf and SOC2-snapshot.pdf for your security team.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Sam West <sam.west@optirail.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Inference ops options and costing questions

Naomi — thanks for the summary and for the materials on the call. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Token pattern: the 100M is an expected monthly average once we go live, but our traffic is spiky. Typical weekday peaks are ~3x baseline for 20–90 minutes, usually 2–3 times/day during operations shifts. Weekend load is ~40% of weekday.
2) Latency: p95 target of ~200–250ms for the inference step is ideal. For hosted, we can tolerate a short tail during extreme peaks but prefer no cold-starts during peak windows.
3) Security/procurement: procurement wants a clear option for a VPC/on-prem deployment if needed — timeline for decision is ~end of July. Procurement also asked for an outline of reserved commit discounts vs pay-as-you-go.

Can you include an apples-to-apples cost example for:
A) Hosted: 100M tokens/month typical with 3x 1-hour spikes 3x/day
B) Dedicated: reserved capacity to handle peak tail (brief description of commit tiers)
C) Private/VPC: one-time setup estimate + monthly support fee

Also: who should procurement loop in for contract/legal questions?

— Sam

Head of Product Ops | OptiRail Inc

Subject: RE: Inference ops options and costing questions

Sam — looping in a quick costing sketch. High level notes and ballpark numbers (will refine once we have exact token composition and model selection):

Hosted (per-token):
- Assumptions: mixed generation/embedding usage, 100M tokens/mo baseline with spikes as described.
- Cost: $0.0008 per generation token (example tier) => ~ $80k/mo on baseline. Spikes are absorbed by autoscaling; burst cost scales linearly.
- Pros: near-zero ops, fast time-to-market. Cons: higher marginal cost during sustained heavy usage.

Dedicated (reserved commit):
- Model: monthly committed GPU pool with peak capacity sizing. Example tiers: 1) Small commit (2x A100-equivalent) - $48k/mo, 2) Medium (4x) - $88k/mo, 3) Large (8x) - $160k/mo.
- If your steady-state maps to Medium, per-token equivalent is ~ $0.00045/token; better economics as volume grows.
- Pros: predictable latency, unit-cost improvements. Cons: commit required; less flexible on deep bursts beyond pool capacity unless configured with burst credits.

Private/VPC (one-time + monthly):
- One-time integration/installation (networking, KMS): $45k–$90k depending on on-prem vs cloud VPC complexity.
- Monthly platform support & reserved capacity: starts at $10k/mo + reserved GPU pricing (similar to Dedicated but with additional infra ops fee).
- Pros: full control, compliance alignment. Cons: longer time-to-production and higher initial cost.

I uploaded a short spreadsheet that maps the three scenarios to your 100M tokens with the 3x spikes: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1aB-opti-rail-estimate (editable). Attached also: redwood-costing-sketch.xlsx for offline review.

Questions for you that will materially change numbers: token mix (generation vs embed/ret), model size (7B, 13B, 70B), and whether you want burst credit pools for dedicated. If you’d like, we can run a quick cost-sensitivity table in the next doc pass.

If procurement wants to talk contract/legal, please loop in procurement@optirail.com and I’ll have our legal lead (legal@redwood.com) join.

– Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
